requirement:
The Rust outline profile under {cite}`requirements.references.outlines` MUST
identify items by segments describing their syntactic ancestry within the file,
such as `fn[run]`, `struct[Packet]`, and `mod[local]/fn[run]`, and MUST NOT
resolve Rust modules across files. Functions, methods, structs, enums, unions,
traits, impls, modules, macros, constants, statics, type aliases, and extern
blocks MUST be outline nodes. Impl segments MUST be named by their syntactic self
type and optional trait path, as `impl[Thing]` and `impl[Thing/Trait]`. `use`
declarations and other items without a suitable name MUST be anonymous. Selector
spelling MUST be documented.
rationale:
**Verdict: the requirement is met.** The implementation is complete and marked, the profile is documented, and the tests cover the listed item kinds and the main edge cases.

**Implementation (`src/outline/rust.rs`)**
- `KINDS` maps every item kind the requirement lists to an outline node:
  - `function_item` and `function_signature_item` become `fn`. This covers functions, methods, trait methods and foreign functions.
  - `struct_item`, `enum_item`, `union_item`, `trait_item` and `mod_item` become `struct`, `enum`, `union`, `trait` and `mod`, each named by its `name` field.
  - `impl_item` becomes `impl`.
  - `macro_definition` is a named `macro`, and `macro_invocation` is an anonymous `macro`.
  - `const_item`, `static_item`, `type_item` and `associated_type` become `const`, `static` and `type`.
  - `foreign_mod_item` becomes `extern`.
  - `use_declaration` is anonymous.
- Selector names come from the tree-sitter field names. Each node's segment is therefore its own name and its syntactic ancestors, so nested selectors such as `mod[local]/fn[run]` and `fn[outer]/fn[inner]` fall out of the shared outline builder.
- Module declarations like `mod external;` are just local `mod` nodes. Nothing in the Rust profile follows them to other files, so modules are not resolved across files.
- `impl_name` names an impl by the text of its `type` field, plus the `trait` field when present. This gives `impl[Thing]` and `impl[Thing/Trait]`, and `impl[Wrapper<T>/Trait]` for a generic impl.
- `impl_name` also reports where the name starts, for the declared-on-line queries.
- `extern_name` names an extern block by its ABI string, and by `Rust` when there is none.
- `in_item_list` and `item_macro` restrict anonymous macro nodes to item position, so macros inside function bodies are not nodes. The requirement lists macros as outline nodes and calls for anonymity where there is no suitable name, so this fits.
- `use_declaration` and `macro_invocation` use `NameRule::Anonymous`, as required.
- The `extern-crate` kind is not in the requirement's list, but it is a named item. The outlines requirement allows profiles to map additional kinds, and `KINDS` is also marked `{impl}` for `outlines`, so this is not an unspecified behaviour.
- All `{impl}` references are on the relevant functions and constants, and `PROFILE` wires them in.

**Documentation**
- `md/reference.md` has the "Rust items" section with example selectors and the "Outline profiles" table. The table gives the grammar nodes and name rules per Rust kind.
- The selector spelling section covers percent-encoding, `#N` and `kind@hash`. Selector spelling is therefore documented.

**Tests (`src/outline/tests.rs`)**
- `rust_selectors_follow_syntactic_ancestry` checks selectors for:
  - mod and inline mod, struct, impl, trait impl, and an impl with an odd self type (`impl [u8; 4]`, giving `impl[%5Bu8;%204%5D]`);
  - trait fn and associated type, `extern "C"` and bare `extern` (`extern[Rust]`), nested fn, and duplicates (`#1`, `#2`);
  - macro_rules, union, enum, const, static, type alias and extern crate.
- It also checks that each selector resolves back to its node, that the empty selector resolves to the root, and that an ambiguous or missing selector is an error.
- `selectors_name_syntactic_ancestry_and_duplicates` adds anonymous `use@` selectors and checks that two `use` declarations are distinct.
- `item_macros_are_anonymous_nodes_and_expression_macros_are_not` covers anonymous item macros at the top level, in impls and in mods. It also checks that macros inside function bodies are not nodes, and the generic impl name `impl[Wrapper<T>/Trait]`.
- The wrapped-header and `extern` declared-on-line test covers multi-line impl and extern naming. The test for the separate module file (`functions_in_a_separate_module_file_are_selected_within_that_file`) covers the no-cross-file-resolution clause through the `selector_inline_and_foreign` example.

No gaps were found, and no FIXMEs are involved.

text: :::{req} rust_item_selectors
The Rust outline profile under {cite}`requirements.references.outlines` MUST
identify items by segments describing their syntactic ancestry within the file,
such as `fn[run]`, `struct[Packet]`, and `mod[local]/fn[run]`, and MUST NOT
resolve Rust modules across files. Functions, methods, structs, enums, unions,
traits, impls, modules, macros, constants, statics, type aliases, and extern
blocks MUST be outline nodes. Impl segments MUST be named by their syntactic self
type and optional trait path, as `impl[Thing]` and `impl[Thing/Trait]`. `use`
declarations and other items without a suitable name MUST be anonymous. Selector
spelling MUST be documented.
:::{req} outlines
Habeas MUST parse Rust, Python, TypeScript, CSS, Markdown, TOML, and YAML
sources with pinned tree-sitter grammars, selected by file extension compared
case-insensitively. A source with any syntax error MUST fail to parse, reporting
the line of its first error. Every
other text file MUST use a plain-text profile in which each line that is not
blank is an anonymous outline node of kind `line`. Each supported language MUST
have an outline profile that maps grammar node kinds to short outline kind names
and, for each mapped kind, states whether a node is named, and by which fields
or children, or anonymous. Only mapped kinds MUST appear in the outline; other
nodes MUST be transparent, so their outline descendants appear under the
nearest outline ancestor. A profile MAY attach grammar siblings to an outline
node, such as Rust attributes and doc comments preceding an item, so the outline
tree need not match the grammar tree exactly; attached siblings are part of that
node for its line range and hash. Every file's outline MUST have a root node
for the whole file, independent of language. Source in no other outline node,
such as top-level statements no profile maps, MUST belong to the root node;
profiles MUST NOT invent fallback kinds for it. Comments MUST NOT be outline nodes. Profiles MUST be
documented. Upgrading a grammar or profile MAY change outlines and MUST be
treated as a deliberate change.
